#3979. Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

The fun stuff that cropped up along the way, avoiding major story spoilers

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:

On this page: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

Yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

It's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar says it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite new features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

Any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

If you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with new statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

When GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the big things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

For now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

#3978. The Cosy Coastal Farming Sim Coral Island Is Officially On Its Way To Switch 2 This December

Update [Thu 19th Nov 2026, 2:55am]: Coral Island's development team has this week announced the co-op farming sim (and its 1.4 Kids Grow Up update) will be launching for Switch 2 on 7th December 2026. Alongside this is a new trailer, which you can check out above.

Original Story: [Sat 17th Oct, 2026 05:05 BST]:

Here on Nintendo Life, we first heard about the laid-back co-op farming sim Coral Island back in 2021, when it successfully hit its Kickstarter goal. Now, after overcoming some roadblocks, it seems it's finally getting a Nintendo release.

This announcement was shared this week during The MIX Fall Showcase, with Stairway Games and Balor Games officially confirming a Switch 2 version will release alongside the free "Kids Grow Up" 1.4 Update in winter 2026.

In this title, inspired by games such as Stardew Valley, you'll be able to experience a "cozy coastal life" either solo or with up to four friends in multiplayer.

Along the way, players can cultivate Starlet Town, protect local landscapes, dive beneath the waves to explore the magical Merfolk Kingdom, and even find love and build a family.

The 1.4 “Kids Grow Up” Update opens a new chapter for Coral Island. Players who choose to embrace parenthood can experience new milestones together as a family as their children grow and develop hobbies and interests of their own. The neighborhood kids are getting older, too, bringing exciting new stories and interactions to Starlet Town.

Farm. Decorate. Craft. Explore. Relax. Players shape their own future—and the future of Coral Island.

So, if this looks like a cosy farming sim you might be interested in, be on the lookout for its arrival on the Switch 2 soon.

#3977. Swarmbreaker is an uncommonly mesmerising tower defence game in which enemies "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid"

It is said that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

In Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!"

"SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

GTA 6 cheat codes let you switch things up in Leonida, but you can't use them until you complete the story

GTA 6 cheats are here to let you cause the maximum amount of chaos possible in Leonida. Whether you're looking to raise up your Wanted Level and unlock infinite ammo just to see what happens, or testing out some base jump locations with no fall damage, cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 are what you're looking for.

A total of 61 GTA 6 cheats are available for PS5 and Xbox Series X, but you won't be able to use any of them right from the beginning of your adventures in Vice City. You need to fully complete Jason and Lucia's main story for cheat codes in GTA 6 to even activate, and from there you have to complete a series of challenges to unlock the codes themselves. It's a lot of work to go through in GTA 6, but trust me, it's worth it in the end.

As expected, once you have activated a cheat in GTA 6 all Trophies or Achievements are disabled for the duration of the play session – the ability to save the game will be disabled too. But with all of that out of the way, here are the GTA 6 cheats we have found so far.This guide is in-progress and will be updated as more GTA 6 cheat codes are unlocked.

GTA 6 cheats are only accessible after you complete all of the main missions. Once you've wrapped up Jason and Lucia's story, open the main menu with the touchpad or menu button and then press R1/RB to navigate to the Progress tab. In there you'll find a new option for Cheats in GTA 6 that wasn't there before.

GTA 6 cheats will not work until you have completed Jason and Lucia's story, regardless of whether you know the code already.

Using Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats is easy enough. While you're in free-roam, all you have to do is press Up on the D-pad to pull out your phone. From that main phone screen, you then need to hold L1/LB and R1/RB together at the same time, before inputting the relevant GTA 6 cheat code with the D-pad to activate it.

#3975. Layoffs Hit XCOM Dev as It Struggles with Production of Third Entry

A third of Firaxis staff to lose their job

XCOM and Midnight Suns studio Firaxis Games has lost roughly one-third of its workforce in a round of layoffs today.

Around 60 people lost their jobs, and studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving the developer.

In a statement, a spokesperson said the team is "restructuring and recentering" around "designing world class strategy games". As a result, Firaxis is being downsized to focus on "design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

Quite how cutting one-third of your overall staff only now means you can refocus on making the best strategy games in the business makes little sense to me.

Apparently, the developer does actually have a third XCOM game in the works, but it's been hit with development issues. The Bloomberg report from Jason Schreier said Firaxis Games missed a "significant milestone over the summer".

Development of the game continues, but it may be affected by today's layoffs.

#3974. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy releases in January, leaving not very long to prepare for all the crunchy cRPG choices and secret wars it'll lob your way

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the not so far away future

Oh shit, that's not too far away. Terrifyingly, that last sentence is now a thing I can accurately write about games coming out in January 2027. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy has just been confirmed as one such game, with the cRPG's heresy investigation set to commence towards the end of the month.

January 28th, 2027, is the full Dark Heresy release date, as announced by devs Owlcat on Steam. The beta version of the game'll be closing down on January 7th to make way for the full game, so as of writing there's still some time to give that a go if you fancy.

If this is the first you've heard of Dark Heresy, here's Owlcat's synopsis of what it's all about:

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the far future in a cRPG set in the rich Warhammer 40,000 universe. Start your service as an acolyte of the Inquisition: Investigate heresy, command a diverse warband, and shape the fate of the Calixis Sector in a story-rich experience where every decision has weight, justice is non-existent, and the line between salvation and damnation is razor-thin. Explore an in-depth depiction of the Inquisition as an organisation and the vast force it commands: its power, bureaucracy, and inner conflicts laid bare like never before.

As an Inquisitor, you have one primary goal: to protect the Imperium, whether that be from the taint of xenos, the betrayal of heretics, or the scourge of mutants, by any means necessary. Be the conduit of the Emperor’s will in a place where all hope was lost decades ago, explore the mysteries of the maddening Tyrant Star, and overcome the worst horrors thrown at you by the Noctis Aeterna.

A place where all hope was lost decades ago? You sure this is the Warhammerverse and not real life lads? I jest, but bursting into rooms and shouting 'Nobody expects the God-Emperor’s inquisition!' Monty Python-style does sound quite fun. Oisin's previously written in more depth about what Dark Heresy devs have said regarding what to expect from its investigations, if you want nitty-gritty details rather than references to sketch comedy.

If you're so inclined, Dark Heresy is wishlistable on Steam.

#3973. GTA 6 Comparison Shows Difference Between Xbox Series X And Series S

Here's how Grand Theft Auto 6 looks across both Xbox consoles

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 3:19pm]: Digital Foundry has also shared an analysis of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S today, and you can watch their video at the bottom of this article. We've covered it in more depth elsewhere on Pure Xbox too:

News Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

Feature GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?

Digital FoundryResolution, performance and visual settings compared.

Original Story: With GTA 6 reviews now out in the wild, and countless Xbox players already getting access to it via the controversial New Zealand trick, it's no surprise that we've also got loads of screenshots and clips doing the rounds online.

One of the best sources for raw Xbox gameplay footage is the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, and they're already uploaded their initial look at both the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of GTA 6.

On Xbox Series X, it's very much what you'd expect - a really amazing-looking game with an internal resolution of 1440p, upscaled to 4K. The 30FPS performance is largely smooth, but does drop frames on occasion.

I also played GTA 6 on Xbox Series X for our Pure Xbox review, and here's what I said about it:

"Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well..."

"It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences."

On Xbox Series S, GTA 6 still looks really impressive from a visual standpoint, even though some drawbacks have clearly been made in terms of ray tracing and texture quality. The frame rate in the game's initial opening is shown to be a locked 30FPS in some sequences, dropping into the mid-20s during busier moments.

Overall though, the feedback we've seen from Xbox Series S players thus far has been very positive, especially in terms of how impressive the game looks. Rockstar Games actually talked to Wccftech about the Series S version as well, revealing they're using AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to scale the resolution to 1080p.

"On the Xbox Series S, we’re starting from a base resolution of 720p, which is scaled to 1080p using AMD FSR Upscaling 4."

"...[our] focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming."

Great stuff, then! We'll leave you with the comparison footage for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S down below.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Feature 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

The fun stuff that cropped up along the way, avoiding major story spoilers

Are you playing on either console yet? What do you think of the visuals and performance? Tell us in the comments.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

You can build (or neglect) the romance and relationship between Jason and Lucia in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Romance in GTA 6 isn't something you should shy away from. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as the pair reunite in Leonida. Whether they stick to being partners in crime or develop a healthy relationship status in GTA 6 is completely up-to you, with the connection between the two playable characters strengthening or weakening depending on your approach to the world. Jason and Lucia's relationship status isn't determined by completing certain missions or ticking off a few optional objectives, but rather it can change based on your actions, choices, and the time you spend together. Small acts of everyday affection and kindness will grow a healthier relationship in GTA 6, while ignoring your partner will slowly drive them apart.

There are four relationship statuses in GTA 6. You can move between each status at any time, organically depending on how you choose to play. You can track Jason and Lucia's relationship status at any time by holding right on the d-pad or by heading into the Jason & Lucia menu. They are (from least to most):

Tip: Jason and Lucia will remain connected as criminal partners throughout all of the GTA 6 missions, regardless of how their romantic relationship develops. However, certain moments in the story and interactions with characters may change depending on their relationship status at the time.

The process of building up your GTA 6 relationship status is organic – it happens gradually, over time through daily acts of affection and small acts of kindness. It's the smallest things that can make a difference, like greeting your partner when you meet up, buying them a snack, restocking their ammunition at an Ammu-Nation, or by holding hands while you explore the city together.

The bond between Jason and Lucia can also improve if you take time to do different activities together. Completing robberies and hitting gang hideouts together will strengthen their relationship, as will doing workouts together at the gym, and enjoying sports and leisure activities as a couple.

A little heart icon will appear on the screen beneath your health bar if you do something that your partner appreciates. Here's just a few examples of ways to improve your relationship status in GTA 6:

Tip: There are loads of ways to interact with your partner and collaborate in the world, more of which we detail in our guide to switching characters in GTA 6.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

To have the strongest relationship in GTA 6, both Jason and Lucia need to contribute to it. You can switch characters by holding right on the d-pad and then pressing R1. If you prioritize playing as one character over the other while you're playing, don't be surprised if the relationship naturally begins to degrade – this will impact the story and interactions between the two in a myriad of ways.

If you'd like to take more deliberate actions to lower your relationship status in GTA 6, then you certainly can do so. If you start ignoring your partner's calls and messages, don't be surprised if they start getting a little short with you on WhatUp. Spending lots of time apart, abandoning your partner while traveling together, or otherwise failing to engage with them on a daily basis will drive the two apart.

Tip: Small acts of affection will always help to improve the bond between Jason and Lucia, but if one of them has a GTA 6 Criminal Profile of 'Irredeemable' the relationship may never recover.

No, you cannot romance other characters beyond Lucia and Jason, at least through my experiences. I played through GTA 6 for over 100 hours and have yet to encounter any real opportunity to form a relationship or romance with any characters beyond those two, suggesting that their relationship is not an open one.

#3971. Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

So long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the big national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have plans for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Currently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the big money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

The next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

Except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

#3970. "BMXing Tanuki Game" Was Prepared For GTA 6's Launch, But Wasn't Expecting Zelda

Ocarina's remake arrived a week before Tanuki: Pon's Summer

November is a huge month for video games, with not only the release of the Ocarina of Time remake but also the long-awaited (and highly anticipated) arrival of GTA 6 this week.

While most games decided to avoid this month, one other title that has been released over the past week is TANUKI: Pon's Summer. If you are wondering why a game starring a BMX-riding tanuki decided to go up against these two juggernauts, it seems the Zelda news caught it by surprise.

Although it was prepared for GTA 6's arrival, Nintendo only announced the release of Ocarina's remake in September, and then launched it at the start of November. Here's what Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards had to say about this during an interview with Games Industry:

"While we originally decided on October to launch, due to marketing opportunities with first-party platforms, we decided that the sweet spot would be just clear of GTA 6's initial launch period. What I don't think we could have accounted for was Nintendo shadow-dropping the release of Ocarina of Time [on November 5]."

He further notes how there's "probably a fair bit more of an overlap with "Switch 2 Zelda players" for Tanuki than there would be for GTA 6". Despite this, there's hope the title can still find "long-term" success through "word-of-mouth" style marketing, and that maybe some players will pick up the "BMXing Tanuki game" once they're done with Nintendo and Rockstar's games.

We gave Tanuki: Pon's Summer seven out of ten stars in our NL review, describing it as a cosy game you can get lost in.

Review TANUKI: Pon's Summer (Switch 2) - Cosy Postie Delivers Sick BMX Tricks & Minigames

Will you be making time for this game at some point? Are you planning to check out any other smaller titles during this busy time of year? Let us know in the comments.

[source gamesindustry.biz, via gonintendo.com]

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters.

#3969. GTA 6 Nominated for Game of the Year Before PS5 Reviews Are Released

We got GTA 6 nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards before GTA 6.

The Game Awards 2026 has just announced the nominees across all its categories, and sticking out like a sore thumb is GTA 6.

It's the odd one out, because it's the only game shortlisted that has yet to release. Despite the fact it isn't out yet — and even that reviews have yet to land — Rockstar's hotly anticipated game is nominated across numerous categories.

In fact, it's the most-nominated game at this year's awards, with a total of eight nods if you include Manni L. Perez's nomination for Best Performance. It's up for the following trophies:

Yes, on top of all its other nominations, GTA 6 is in contention for Game of the Year.

There has been much debate online about whether the game would be considered for The Game Awards at all, given how close its launch is to the event itself.

Many believed it would not receive any nominations, because the nominee announcement was set to occur before GTA 6 launches.

However, the voting jury — which comprises hundreds of gaming media outlets from around the world — has deemed the game worthy of recognition in eight categories, more than any other 2026 title.

What's clear is that many jury members must have played the game, but more interesting is that they clearly hold it in high regard if it's been shortlisted for so many awards.

This has been quite revealing, then; it's a big hint at what critics think of the game, and we now also know (officially) who is playing the role of Lucia Caminos, one of the two lead characters.

#3968. Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

So, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest."

If I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Big Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together."

Three screens will show you more of Avengers: Doomsday

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Avengers: Doomsday is coming to the three-screen sensory overload that is ScreenX, with directors Anthony and Joe Russo promising a more complete look at the upcoming Marvel movie in the format.

"Avengers: Doomsday is massive," Anthony Russo began in a video from ScreenX. "From the beginning, we wanted audiences to experience the scale of this movie in the most impressive ways."

Joe Russo added, "We worked closely with the ScreenX team to design a version of the film specifically for this format, expanding the world of Doomsday beyond the main screen."

Then, Anthony Russo revealed ScreenX's unique selling point for fans who are aiming to be Avengers: Doomsday completionists: "You'll see things in ScreenX you simply will not see anywhere else."

As per Cineworld, the 12-projector setup of ScreenX is a "state-of-the-art atmospheric experience [that] surrounds you in your seat with innovative 270° projection across 3 screens, blended into 1 unforgettable projection experience."

Avengers: Doomsday will be available in multiple formats, including Marvel's own InfinityVision. IMAX screeners are expected to be available in early 2027 – thanks to Dune 3's exclusivity over the format.

Expect to see some intense thrills up on the big screen, too. The confirmed Avengers: Doomsday age rating has it locked in at PG-13 but, for the first time ever in an Avengers movie, will include "bloody images."

Avengers: Doomsday sees Fantastic Four, Fox's X-Men, and the MCU's Avengers team up to stop the twin threats of universe-ending incursions and the emergence of Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. With Hulk and Scarlet Witch seemingly already by his side, we might need those extra screens to see the sheer amount of Avengers who will be needed to stop this almighty threat.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18.

#3966. Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.

Feature GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?

Digital FoundryResolution, performance and visual settings compared.

Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.

This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.

Digital Foundry reckons that the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 is a great-looking game for the most part, highlighting things like lighting, reflections and even the incredible hair system, while also pointing out minor downsides such as missing shadows and occasionally blurry appearances. They also reckon that the frame rate generally maintains its 30FPS target, but will slip in busy situations like chases and explosions.

"Generally speaking, the game acquits itself quite well on Microsoft's senior current-gen console. Visual settings seem pretty solid across the board."

The Xbox Series S version is also said to be pretty good in the graphical department, retaining the core features that make GTA 6 such a great game visually. It's the frame rate that bothers DF the most, as it's much more variable and prone to falling below its 30FPS target. That said, it appears to hover around 25-30FPS for the most part.

"Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land."

If you're wondering which console is the absolute best to play GTA 6 on, it's unsurprisingly the PS5 Pro. Nevertheless, Digital Foundry says that both the Xbox Series X and the PS5 versions "look and play well" despite their softer image (and the Series X is actually "slightly smoother" when setting the Xbox to 120Hz with a VRR display), while the Xbox Series S version is the "hardest to recommend" despite its surprisingly impressive visuals.

"In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through."

Both the video and the website article are totally different from each other, so it's worth watching / reading the pair of them and getting a better idea of how GTA 6 fares across both Xbox consoles (and PS5 for that matter).

In my experience, I've found GTA 6 to be fantastic on Xbox Series X across the board for the most part, and while the Series S version is clearly a little more unstable, I'd wager that most players will still be perfectly happy with it.

#3965. Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the new mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

It's a "stopgap solution" while the site's staff are busy "working on more sophisticated tools"

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon."

Cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is important for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the issue for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected."

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

Personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

#3963. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now just hours away! We're in the final home stretch now, with availability rolling out on PS5 worldwide within the next 24 hours.

As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.

When the game launches in the UK, we'll have a hub live on the home page documenting our coverage and providing a place for you to share your first experiences with GTA 6.

GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

If you were to play GTA 6 early via the New Zealand method detailed above, you get access to the game at these times:North America: 3am PST / 4am MST / 5am CST / 6am ESTUK/Ire: 11am GMTEurope: 12pm CET / 1pm EETAsia/Oceania: 8pm JST / 7pm AWST / 10pm AEDT

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

Rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

Have you pre-ordered GTA 6, and will you be staying up to play at midnight? Let us know in the comments below.

The additional content you unlock through pre-ordering GTA 6 or buying the Ultimate Edition is all found in different locations

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Are you wondering how to unlock the GTA 6 pre-order and GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses? Don't worry, I was too through my first few hours in Leonida. It turns out that Rockstar Games doesn't want you having too many cool things too quickly, which is why you'll need to progress through different sections of the game before you'll gain access to unique weapons, vehicles, mod shops, clothing stores, and more that come as part of the DLC package, no matter which of the GTA 6 versions you own.

Below you'll find a breakdown of where to get the GTA 6 pre-order bonuses for both the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition of the game. You'll also find a detailed breakdown of where to access all of the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition exclusives, which unlock as you progress through the story.

Regardless of whether you pre-ordered the Standard Edition or the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, you'll get access to a couple of nice bonus items. These are available from Chapter 3 onwards, and can be unlocked by doing the following:

The option to collect a uniquely-styled '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle from Vice Beach will appear as a task within the Exploration section of the map index. Once you've collected the vehicle from outside the Ocean View Hotel, you'll also unlock the Bonita Court Garage north of Washington Beach to store it in.

Once you've collected your '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle, you'll unlock some other bonuses as well. Head back to your residence and access the wardrobe to find exclusive outfits, and then visit any Salon to access a new hairstyle for Jason and Lucia under the Special section of the in-store menu.

As soon as you've found the 55 Vapid Stainer, the first thing you'll want to do is drive across to any Ammu-Nation store. Once inside, access the weapons locker and head into the Cosmetics / Wraps section of the modify menu on any gun to freely apply the pre-order exclusive weapon pattern.

If you purchase the more expensive GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, you'll find that Rockstar has well and truly made it worth your while. The exclusive storefronts, weapons, clothes, and vehicles aren't immediately accessible, instead they become available once you reach certain GTA 6 mission milestones:

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Once you're able to leave Jason's House in Chapter 1, you'll find two exclusive vehicles waiting for you. Underneath the house you'll find an Army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle in the driveway, and off to the back of the building you'll spot a Crest Kayak which can be used to explore the Leonida Keys.

Only available for use in Chapter 1, you can get an exclusive pro build for Jason's Vapid Ganado pickup truck. Open up the map and head into the Vehicles index, from there click the Mod Shops option and look for Coastal Auto Care in Key Lento. Drive the Vapid Ganado over there and the unlock can be applied inside the Pro Builds / Full Kits section of the mod shop menu.

Take Jason to any Ammu-Nation store from Chapter 1 and access the weapon locker to unlock a personalized Girardi ES9 pistol. You can do the same with Lucia from Chapter 2 onwards, unlocking a unique Klose K17 pistol. Both of these weapons are free to equip and use.

Once you're into Chapter 2 of GTA 6, you'll be able to access unique weapon variants of the powerful Morgan revolver (regardless of whether you've already purchased the weapon). Jason and Lucia have their own versions, which can be accessed from any Ammu-Nation weapon locker.

Located in North Leonard County, just north of Lake Leonida, you'll gain access to One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop from Chapter 1. This GTA 6 Mod Shop specializes in off-road vehicles, and will give you access to a range of custom, hand-painted liveries for purchase.

Spend enough time meeting the locals at the Motel safehouse and you'll eventually meet Wyman, who will invite Lucia to the Thrillbilly Mud Club. Once you've completed a Dirt Track Race, look for a task in the exploration section of the map index to go collect your Dominator buggy and storage garage.

Once you have collected the Dominator buggy in Chapter 2, Wyman will contact you on WhatUp and ask for your help tracking down parts for classic cars. Look for the Find Cars for Wyman option in the exploration section of the map index to start this optional activity.

If you've got money to burn, then you'll want to take your favorite car over to Rideout Customs, located in the Crosstown district of Vice City. This Mod Shop offers unique interiors, rims, and stylings for any Donks vehicle classes. Head to the Vehicles map index and click the Mod Shops tab to set a destination.

Technically accessible from Chapter 1, there's a number of PTT YOUNGIN$ Compounds to raid for cash and key valuables. You'll need to head into Southside (south of Vice Dale County) to unlock these Illegal Operations. Once you've visited the area, head to the Robberies section of the map index.

Stock 305 can be found in the north quadrant of Vice City, in the Stockyard district. This skate store, selling contemporary streetwear and accessories, can be easily located by opening the map, heading to the style section of the index, and clicking onto the Casual & Street tab to get a destination.

Undoubtedly one of the better Hair & Beauty locations in GTA 6, Sara's Unisex Salon is located on the main strip of the Hamlet town. Find it in the Style section of map index. Once you're into Chapter 2, you'll gain access to exclusive signature looks for Jason and Lucia.

Located in the Stockyard area of Vice City, the Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is open for business from Chapter 1. This tattoo parlor has over 50 signature tattoos for Jason and Lucia, all designed by the artist collective FAILE. Head to the Style section of the map index and look for the Tattoos tab.

The Wonder Whale is a Souvenir & Swimwear shop available for all players, located in the heart of the Key Leonto area (just off the main strip of highway). Head to the mannequins in the store to find some exclusive merch to purchase and wear. Just head to the Style section of the map index to get a location.

Once you're in Chapter 4, you've likely figured out the styles of both Jason and Lucia. Expect that to be challenged once a set of outfits are unlocked, for free – accessed directly from your wardrobe. A new set of tattoos are also available from most tattoo parlors, and new hair/beard styles at Sara's Unisex Salon.

Chapter 4 will also unlock a Shitzu Squalo for you to use for fishing and to search for dive sites in GTA 6. The boat is docked in a canal, south of the Washington Beach area of the map – just to the left of the Y Hotel. You can locate this vehicle at all times by heading to the Personal section of the map index.

An exclusive variant of one of the best cars in GTA 6 will be made available to you in Chapter 5. The '95 Grotti Cheetah is parked up in the garage beneath the Pegassi Residences building just waiting for you to collect it. You can also find a task in the Exploration section of the map index to help locate it.

#3961. Skydance Games lay off an undisclosed number of staff in the wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, in latest case of consolidation killing livelihoods

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

#3960. Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

There's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

#3959. Multiple Games Are Available Today On Xbox, Including One With GTA & Zelda Inspirations (November 18)

Just in case you wanted a break from the GTA news, we thought we'd remind you that we've got a few games either releasing or being added to Xbox Game Pass today, and there's some interesting stuff in the mix here.

The one that catches the eye is Vice: Magic City Mayhem, which we mentioned recently in our article about two Vice City games releasing in mid-November. While the cover art is very GTA-inspired, and it's set in a world with a "Vice City theme", it actually appears to have more in common with classic Zelda in terms of the gameplay style.

It's also a very temporary Xbox and and Epic Games Store exclusive, as the Steam, PS5 and Nintendo Switch versions have been slightly delayed for whatever reason.

News Xbox Suddenly Has Two Vice City Games Releasing In Mid-November

This one's based on Zelda with GTA influences!

Beyond this, three games are being added to the Xbox Game Pass Premium service today, with High on Life 2 arguably being the highlight (if you enjoy the kind of humour it throws at you). The other two are Call of the Elder Gods and Roadside Research, which are both worth a play as well.

GTA 6 is technically already out in some countries as well (such as New Zealand), but its official release date is November 19th rather than the 18th, so we'll highlight it in tomorrow's article instead.

We'll throw all of today's new Xbox releases and Xbox Game Pass additions down below.

Vice: Magic City Mayhem is a top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme. Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

Turn-based management roguelike. Command the Inquisition and rule an industrial city on the empire’s edge. Use your train to meet prisoner shipment quotas by hunting heretics and slaying magical beasts. Produce supplies, contain revolt, and sacrifice prisoners to stop the madness.

An intergalactic conspiracy threatens the fate of humanity! Team up with a wide cast of talking alien guns as you shoot, stab, and skate your way through the exotic locales to take down the bad guys and save your favorite species (humans)!

Journey to the far corners of the Earth and unearth ancient horrors in this Lovecraftian narrative puzzle adventure and sequel to 2020’s critically acclaimed Call of the Sea.

Roadside Research is a 1 to 4 player co-op gas station simulator. Except you’re aliens. And undercover. Do very human things like restocking shelves while preparing for the invasion. Just don’t get caught.

"Yes," indeed, a Blade Runner game might be underway

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Blade Runner 2099 isn't here just yet, with Amazon Prime's new take on the iconic cinematic cyberpunk universe set to arrive on November 25 – but its producers are already discussing a potential video game, apparently.

News of the possible game comes directly from IGN, who learns from Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson – Blade Runner 2099 executive producers and co-CEOs of Blade Runner franchise owner Alcon Entertainment – that, "yes," it might be underway somewhere down the line. And, furthermore, the two emphasize that it'll be a "AAA" project if anything, meaning this won't be a small fish situation… It may be the Blade Runner game.

Although Kosove and Johnson couldn't give much more information on the mysterious (possible, as it seems now) game, they do stress how important allowing players "interact" with the cyberpunk universe will be. It is, after all, a level of immersion Blade Runner's not really featured before, despite having been in the limelight in some shape or form since its 1982 debut film – the Ridley Scott classic that started it all.

I do wonder what the Blade Runner game might look like, should it come to fruition, though. Will it be akin to Cyberpunk 2077 – an RPG that leans heavily on player choice but builds its own universe with unique characters, standing comfortably separate from its tabletop source material – or shall it feature faces familiar to longtime fans (perhaps even those introduced in Blade Runner 2099 next week)? Only time will tell.

Regardless, it's an exciting time to be a fan of the gritty, sci-fi cyberpunk genre, if you ask me. Between CD Projekt Red's own confirmed Cyberpunk 2 and now a potential Blade Runner game, there's plenty for players to anticipate.

#3957. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#3956. GTA 6 Requires New PS5 Firmware Update to Play

As we reported early yesterday, PS5 has a new firmware update, numbered v14.23.00. It’s now confirmed you’ll need to have this installed to play GTA 6.

Notifying players on social media, a PlayStation Support page said: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing GTA 6. Players should download this update prior to midnight on 19th November so that they’re ready to play on launch day, 19th November.”

Sony usually gives users a period of grace to play their games before a new firmware update is made mandatory, so this is unprecedented behaviour.

But the stakes have never been higher either: Rockstar’s open world is the most anticipated game of all time, and it’s coming at a time when the PS5 has been cracked wide open.

Sony’s currently in a cat-and-mouse battle with hackers, as it tries to shore up the security of its console.

That all comes at the cost of inconvenience to the rest of us, as we’re forced to install firmware updates which have been coming more and more frequently of late.

This latest version is just 1.3GB so it’s not a huge lift, but this is your 24 hour warning that you’ll need to have it installed to play GTA 6.

#3955. "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers."

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote."

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

If you've turned on your Xbox console today and been presented with a background for GTA 6 without selecting it, there's a reason for that. Xbox is promoting the game by making a default "event" background for certain people.

You can let it sit there and do its thing if you want (although unfortunately it's not dynamic), or you can turn it off by going to Settings, Personalisation, My Background and then unticking the "show event-themed backgrounds" box.

In addition to this, Xbox has added a brand-new dynamic background for Halo: Campaign Evolved today, and it actually looks really, really cool. I might be rocking this background for a while to be honest!

Those who haven't been keeping track might also notice an Xbox 25 dynamic background that serves to celebrate Xbox's 25th anniversary. You'll find all of these by going to Settings, Personalisation, My Background and then browsing through the Dynamic Backgrounds that are on offer.
