Grand Theft Auto 6 is not on PC so I can't review it. But somehow I, a member of PC Gamer, got access to GTA 6 before it launched. For the past two weeks I've secretly sunk approximately 100 hours in it (on something called a PlayStation 5) and now, finally, I can talk about it. What a relief.

So this isn't a review, but I can give a verdict of sorts:

It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC.

I guess I shouldn't be surprised by just how massive and detailed the world is. It's Rockstar: huge open worlds is what they do, and they've had a decade to do it. But I was stunned when I started playing, and a hundred hours later, I'm honestly still pretty stunned. Rockstar said GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's map, but it feels twice as big as "twice as big" should feel. It's enormous.

I'm constantly impressed by the macro and micro of it all. I can step back and take in the sheer size and scale of Leonida: the archipelago representing the Florida keys to the south, the vast wetlands standing in for the Everglades, the dense neighborhoods and shining skyscrapers of Vice City, the miles of beaches and forests and industrial areas and state parks. And I can zoom in and admire the tiny details: the carefully placed clutter and photos and belongings in a stranger's apartment, the accurate mating rituals of two great blue herons in the wild, or the font choice on a printout pinned to the wall of an office cubicle instructing employees on breakroom etiquette.

I've lost hours doing nothing but wandering around the world.

I've lost hours doing nothing but wandering around the world, picking a point in the distance that looked interesting and getting distracted by a dozen other things along the way. Exploration is always rewarding: Sometimes, because I find one of hundreds of collectibles hidden throughout the map, but usually because I happen upon an interesting landmark, spot an animal I haven't seen before, stumble into a mysterious scene or sight (I have found many yet haven't unraveled any of them yet), or have a chance encounter with the seemingly inexhaustible supply of "Florida Man"-style weirdos that populate Leonida.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

My only issue with the world is that present day Miami doesn't hold a lot of interest for me, pop-culture-wise. New York and Los Angeles are fascinating in any era, and I loved the neon-soaked '80s Vice City from Rockstar's game. But GTA 6's Vice City doesn't quite stand up against Liberty City or Los Santos. I'm not saying it's a bad place to spend time: it's an incredible facsimile of the real Miami, with an intense amount of detail and attention paid to the diversity of the city, like its recreation of Little Havana (called Little Cuba here). But it doesn't grab me the way the cities in the last two GTA games did.

It's stressful being in a new relationship. What if my partner texts me and I don't respond right away? Am I giving them enough attention, or too much attention? If they want to hang out, can I say no if I'm busy doing something else? It's been quite a while since I dated IRL, but the early hours of getting to know Jason and Lucia gave me those early relationship jitters I remember so well.

There are lots of systems in GTA 6 for keeping Jason and Lucia's partnership strong: talking to each other, showing affection, doing activities together, and even committing crimes together will improve their bond. That makes it a little tense when one character wants to do something and you (as the other character) don't.

One day as I was playing as Jason, Lucia texted me because she wanted to talk about our financial future. But I was on a speedboat halfway across the map and I had just spotted what I suspect was one of Florida's many cryptids (which, after 100 hours, I still cannot confirm is actually in the game or not). Was I really supposed to drop everything I was doing?

I dropped everything I was doing. Instead of becoming a renowned cryptid investigator, Lucia and I went to the bank to set up a savings account. Was I happy about it? Hell no. I was annoyed. But that felt real to me—not the cryptid part, but the idea of being responsible to your partner. While playing them, both individually and together, I wanted to be a good partner, and sometimes that meant glumly turning around my stolen speedboat and having a frank talk about money. It's pretty cool that a game about robbing banks and blowing up police helicopters could make me want to be a good boyfriend.

The two of them are a satisfying couple to play in other respects, too. When knocking over a jewelry store or check-cashing place (cute date idea), your partner can perform crowd control, keeping security guards and employees docile, while you smash open display cases, empty cash drawers, and crack the safe in the back room. During story missions, the duo is often split up and you bounce between their perspectives, with Jason shooting his way through a crowd of goons in an office tower to Lucia fighting hand-to-hand several floors above.

I had a really wonderful two weeks of ignoring my real life partner while spending quality time with these two.

But the best moments as a duo are when you're coming up with your own ways to play them as a couple. After trying to rip off narcotics from a gang stronghold, I got into a heavy gunfight in a narrow alleyway, and with Lucia on one side and Jason on the other, I was able to fight my way out. As Lucia I could cover Jason as he advanced, and as Jason I could get better angles on the thugs trying to bring Lucia down. It was fluid, fun, and not part of any main mission, just an organic bit of co-op play with me swapping between them as needed. This was the sort of thing that GTA 5 could only pull off in heavily-scripted story missions with its three characters, but here you really are a dynamic duo.

Even more fun? Just hanging out together as a couple. You can take them both to a store to shop for clothes, then compliment each other on their new looks. Or go on a date and play minigolf while gently trash-talking each other. (Tall Jason to short Lucia: "So, is this, like, regular-sized golf to you?") Hit the night clubs and do some dancing. Buy two ice cream cones, hand one to your partner, and enjoy them together. Even just lying in bed, side-by-side, and scrolling your phones is a warm and fuzzy activity amidst all the crime and bloodshed. It's good stuff. I had a really wonderful two weeks of ignoring my real life partner while spending quality time with these two.

Jason and Lucia are a good match for the more deliberate gameplay of GTA 6. Taking a page from Red Dead Redemption 2, your car is basically now your horse: not just a ride, but a gun locker. No longer can you keep a full arsenal in your weapon wheel or unholster a grenade launcher from your back pocket.

The pair can conceal two handguns in their pants, but "long" guns like shotties and rifles are visible on your back or in your hands. This matters: Even the locals of the gun-friendly Leonida will notice and sometimes panic at the sight of a heavily armed maniac, drawing outright alarm from security guards and cops.

So you'll have to stash those big guns in your car until you need them, along with a few changes of clothes because witnesses to your crimes will tell the cops what you're wearing. This makes even a quick, mindless smash-and-grab feel like a mission with phases and choices: scope it out, plan your moves and escape route, grab your gear, and then afterwards, stow your guns and change clothes once the cops are out of sight. When things go sideways, it can be a lot of fun to scramble your way out of the heat: dumping your big guns in an alleyway and running into a clothing shop to buy some new duds, a hat, and sunglasses, so you don't match the description the cops are looking for.

And while you can't play entirely non-lethally, you can at least play less-lethally. Using your focus meter (bullet time) will highlight your enemies' elbows, knees, hands, shoulders, and other non-fatal places to deposit a bullet, so you can incapacitate them instead of just headshotting them if that's how you want to roll. I did a lot of that in my playthrough, partly to keep Jason and Lucia feeling less like murdering psychopaths so that I could continue to like them as characters, but also because it added an extra challenge: aiming carefully at joints instead of just popping lead in every dome I see.

Playing less lethally is another way GTA 6 makes the near-constant violence a bit less mindless, though trust me, my body count was still pretty high by the end of the main story. It's hard to non-lethally shoot down a helicopter with a grenade launcher from the back of a speedboat.

I don't love everything about GTA 6. The big action setpieces, while technically impressive, usually wind up feeling pretty samey: pull a big score, everything goes wrong, 100 guys show up, shoot all of them in the knees, then drive away, 100 cars show up, shoot all of them them in the tires (tires are a car's knees), escape. Rockstar missions are still Rockstar missions.

As with RDR2, these moments of front-page bombast contradict the fantasy of small-time outlaws struggling to get ahead, and GTA 6 goes full ridiculous with Fast and Furious-style mayhem. I'm not saying those sequences aren't entertaining, they just clash with the story of a couple of star-crossed crooks trying to save up enough money to get out of the game. And after you've shot your hundredth kneecap of the night, it gets a bit tiresome.

As for the story and characters? It's Rockstar, so some of it is genuinely good but a lot of it is exaggerated bluster. Lucia has some interactions with a family member that feel pretty real and there's a duo of rappers who are fun to spend time with, but I found the majority of the supporting characters either too grating or one-dimensional to care much about. Luckily, the writing and performances of Jason and Lucia make up for that. I enjoyed spending time with them. They had some raw moments that landed well. I felt feelings. I came to care about this couple.

If this is sounding too grown up, don't worry. There's a subplot about furries. A naked guy got into my car and took a sex toy out of his butt. There's a mission where you have to handle multiple dildos. The rideshare app's logo looks like a penis. All the actual penises also look like a penis, too. Rockstar is still Rockstar.

Now that I'm done with the main story, the real game can begin: just having fun in that big, beautiful sandbox. And I've got lots left to do: while I mentioned minigolf, there are actual, entire golf courses, too (this is Florida, remember).

I've done a bit of scuba diving for treasure but still have dozens of shipwrecks to discover. I don't find hunting much fun—hitscan sniper rifles aren't satisfying to use—but I sure like spotting new animals to check off my list, and there are over 200 of them to find. I've only caught one fish. I haven't done any drone races or stunt flying or base jumping or been to a shooting range. There are several in-game videogames I still have to play and a bunch of in-game TV shows to check out. I've somehow hardly gotten anything done in the two weeks I've been playing.

And this is deeply embarrassing, but I barely own any cars! I'm still mainly driving the muscle car I got very early in the game. It's not that there's not a lot to choose from—there are hundreds of autos to theft—it's that the handling and acceleration and physics of every car is different. That's great, obviously, but I quickly got used to driving a few cars and didn't want to have to learn the quirks of more vehicles while fleeing from the cops. Now that the story is behind me, though, it's finally time to start collecting.

I'm still trying to decide where I'd place GTA 6 among Rockstar's other games. RDR2 remains my favorite, followed by Red Dead Redemption, but do I like GTA 6 more than GTA 5? Ultimately, yeah, I just decided while writing this: I do. I like Jason and Lucia more than the three crooks from GTA 5, and maybe even more than I liked Niko Bellic in GTA 4. It's not entirely down to their personalities and performances, but also the systems Rockstar created to let me play as a couple, that make me feel like I had a co-op partner along for the ride.

I'm still trying to decide where I'd place GTA 6 among Rockstar's other games.

In a game like Skyrim where I can have followers, I almost always play solo. But in GTA 6, I found myself calling my partner to meet up almost every time I went out exploring. The game is better when they're together.

I wish we had some idea of when GTA 6 was coming to PC because after playing almost 100 hours on PS5, I'm desperate to get it on my desktop. I can't wait to see what modders can do with this thing (especially when they fix the weird cheat restrictions). As a PC gamer, I'm dying to aim at people's knees with my mouse instead of a thumbstick. And I'm especially curious to see what Rockstar has planned for an online mode (which they have said nothing about), and how FiveM, which Rockstar now owns, will tie into it. That big, beautiful world will only be better on PC where it belongs.

#3879. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

UPDATE: And the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store history.

UPDATE 11TH NOVEMBER: Grand Theft Auto 6 has also become the most pre-ordered game "of all time" on the Xbox Store, Microsoft has announced. And on that platform, again, the advice is to pre-load because of "unprecedented demand" for the game, a post on Xbox Wire said.

The Xbox difference is that you can use Xbox Cloud to stream GTA 6 to other Xbox devices, although not PC, notably - the game isn't available on PC and presumably Rockstar doesn't want it playable there by any means. Microsoft's stream-deal with Rockstar has also expanded to include Red Dead Redemption 2 "and more", which will be available to stream in the "coming months".

ORIGINAL STORY 10TH NOVEMBER: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

Have you managed to resist pre-ordering it yet?

#3878. The hills are alive with The Sound of Fury, a fantasy musical hack 'n' slash about weaponising pianos to fight the Devil

My firstest-ever Golden Joystick Awards, which took place last night in London, was marred somewhat by 1) a gin & tonic costing eleven quid and 2) my view of the stage being directly obscured by its own rigging. Nonetheless, I did crane enough to get a good view at the reveal of The Sound of Fury, a musically-minded hack 'n' slash in which a troubled classical musician descends into Hell to save a friend from the Devil.

It's not out until late 2027, and the strength of its monster-battering will of course lay in how it feels in the hand. I like the look of this one, though. While it doesn't appear to be a full-on rhythm action game in the Hi-Fi Rush or Dead as Disco vein, it's clearly trying incorporate our glum hero's virtuosity with both visual and thematic flair: spinning attacks are accentuated by trails of sheet music staves, and at least one move inflicts enemies with uncontrollable bouts of dancing. Weapons also take the form of instruments, the trailer being particularly keen to show grand pianos being powerbombed into demon heads. "You dropped your... keys," I will say, to the demons. Heh heh heh.

Also of note is The Sound of Fury's unusual interpretation of Hell, which rather than the usual Biblical/Nordic/Ancient Greek depictions we get in games, is a washed-out mashup of what the Steam page calls "humanity's darkest chapters." Thus, you fight not red-skinned horned imps but gasmasked soldiers and Klu Klux Klansmen, with history-spanning anomalies distorting an otherwise 19th century-flavoured fantasyscape. The laws of time evidently aren't followed here, not least when the protag whips out a Flying V guitar to give the Grim Reaper a different kind of axe wound.

I can't find much else out about developers and self-publishers Games By Wojtek, with that pluralisation assuming 'they' aren't just one person named Wojtek, but The Sound of Fury looks to be his/their debut game. Hopefully it gets a demo, in due course, so we can try tickling its ivories ourselves.

#3877. Guide: GTA 6: Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know. This spoiler-free GTA 6 guide includes info on a dozen key features and mechanics that will help you make the best start to your life in Vice City.

On this page: GTA 6 Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:

GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.

Press Options and select Settings > Gameplay. Scroll to the bottom (options 24 and 25) and you can choose to enable Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, as shown:

Accessible Combat will both reduce the damage you take in gunfights, while increasing the damage enemies receive, making firefights much more manageable.

Reduced Vehicle Damage, meanwhile, will reduce the damage your car takes when in crashes or combat. This means there's less chance of your car becoming difficult to control or exploding.

The game will warn you that enabling these "changes the balance and experience of gameplay", meaning your experience will be a lot easier. Using them does not alter the story or disable Trophies, however.

GTA 6 has a new control scheme which modernises its gameplay by mapping run to L3 and jump to Cross/X.

For those of you who've spent over a decade playing GTA 5 and GTA Online, however, you may prefer to use Rockstar's more traditional control scheme.

Fortunately, this is relatively easy to enable.

Press Options and select Settings > Control Scheme, as pictured:

The control scheme will automatically be set to the new Default layout, but you can toggle to Classic if you prefer the GTA 5 approach.

As its name implies, GTA 6 is all about grand theft auto — or, in other words, stealing cars.

Most vehicles you find parked around Vice City will be locked, but it is possible to steal them quicker with a very simple tip.

When the minigame for any criminal activites appear — like using your Slim Jim, Clone Key, or even hotwiring a car — there's a pink "sweet spot" you can find to speed up the action:

This makes it quicker to break in and make a quick getaway.

Just move the sticks around to find the right spot, and use those extra seconds wisely to escape swiftly:

GTA 6 has a living, breathing open world that encourages exploration. If you take the time to look around, you'll almost certainly discover something to do.

However, if you want to continue with the story and you're not sure what to do next, there's a way to easily see your next objective or story mission.

Press the Touch Pad to open your map and then using the index on the left of the screen, press Right to see a list of available story missions, with mandatory objectives at the top and optional ones listed below:

You can immediately set a waypoint to any mission with Cross/X.

There is no traditional fast travel in GTA 6, but there is a way you can get around the map quickly for a nominal fee.

Bring up your smartphone by pressing Up and select RydeMe:

You'll need to have an active waypoint, which you can choose from within the app or by picking one in advance via your map with Touch Pad.

You'll be notified a driver is on the way and you'll be able to see them from your minimap:

Once you get in your Ryde, hold L2 to focus on your driver. You can then hold Triangle to skip your journey for $100 and immediately arrive at your destination:

Longer journeys will cost more than shorter ones, but fast travelling this way is relatively inexpensive overall.

There are two types of money in GTA 6: cash stored in your wallet and money protected in your BuckMe bank. The latter will unlock as part of Chapter 1.

You can see both types of money at any time by pushing Down:

Money stored in your wallet will be lost if you're Busted or Wasted during gameplay, so it's really important you put this in your BuckMe bank.

The easiest way to do this is press Up to access your smartphone and select BuckMe > ATM Finder:

This will automatically select a waypoint to the nearest ATM machine. Follow it and deposit any funds in your wallet into your BuckMe bank, where it'll be safe even if you get arrested or die:

Throughout GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will build a criminal profile which can affect how NPCs and the wider world of Leonida responds to you.

Murdering enemies will contribute towards a more aggressive criminal profile. As such, you may want to consider a non-lethal approach.

One way to do this is by favouring stealth and grabbing enemies with R2, so you can cleanly knock them out without killing them:

Another option, if you get caught up in a gunfight, is to target non-vitals like kneecaps and arms.

You can easily see non-vitals by pressing L3 and R3 and aiming at yellow parts of the body:

You'll know an enemy has been debilitated without killing them if a yellow X appears in your weapon's reticule. A red X will appear if your target has been murdered.

If you need to set a quick waypoint to an important location in GTA 6, you don't necessarily need to press Touch Pad to bring up your map.

Instead, hold Down and you'll get an alternative in-game view of any nearby shops, waypoints, or story missions:

You can highlight any of these and press R3 to automatically set a GPS route to where you want to go.

There'll be times in GTA 6 when you're separated from your car and you want to spawn it nearby.

You can do this by opening your smartphone with Up and selecting the Scooter Bros app:

Select which car you want to use from the app and you'll be charged a fee depending on the delivery distance and your car's current condition:

Your car will then automatically spawn in a nearby location, marked on your minimap:

Stealing or entering a car in GTA 6 does not mean you'll have access to it forever.

You'll need to park it in a Parking Space or Garage to temporarily store it, and register it at a Pay 'N' Spray to keep it forever.

Find a car you want to keep and set a waypoint for a Pay 'N' Spray, like with this Emperor Sultan I just stole:

Drive into the Pay 'N' Spray and select Register to swap the plates. The fee commanded will depend on the value of the car:

Note that you will need free Stored Vehicle slots to register your car. You can sell previous cars directly at the Pay 'N' Spray:

Alternatively, you can press Up to open your smartphone and select Vice City Real Estate. This will let you buy more garages for additional Parking Spots:

This feature becomes available during a story mission, so you may not immediately have access to it if you're still early in the campaign.

Generic upgrades are available for all vehicles at any Mod Shop, but if you want specialist tunings you need to go to the right shop.

These are marked with a blue Wrench icon.

Press Up to open your map and then Right to open the map index.

Select Vehicles > Mod Shops and look for a Mod Shop with a blue Wrench icon, as shown:

Set a waypoint for the appropriate Mod Shop and you'll find all of the customisations and specialised upgrades available for your current vehicle.

Just like in real-life, staying on top of your smartphone notifications in GTA 6 can be time consuming.

Fortunately, the game will mark important messages for you in the Reminders tab:

Press Up to bring up your smartphone and then press Square to access your Reminders.

Here you'll find a curated list of key messages, including in-game news articles and NPCs who are waiting for your replies:

Hopefully you've learned a thing or two with this spoiler-free GTA 6 guide. Are there any other tips and tricks you think the world should should know? Share them in the comments section below.

GTA 6 is now slowly rolling out across the world – or not so slowly, if you use the New Zealand trick – and players are already starting to uncover the game's secrets. I'd give you a spoiler warning here, but you should probably already be on internet blackout if you're concerned about seeing little surprises early. After all, multiple people have already discovered Bigfoot.

It seems that Bigfoot's appearance is tied to a single location in the game, as every player I've come across – whether the clip is on YouTube, Twitter, Reddit, or Instagram – finds him feasting on a bloody deer corpse at a dirt road intersection. If you chase Bigfoot into the woods, you'll likely stumble upon a strange effigy of a person tied to a tree. If you investigate it, you'll soon fall over, see Bigfoot approach as you lose consciousness, and awaken back where you first saw the creature.

found bigfoot in GTA 6 https://t.co/Sa7B6wVmF4November 18, 2026

Bigfoot's got a long history in GTA, going back to the PS2 era. He didn't actually appear in San Andreas, but rumors about his presence there became so prolific that Rockstar would eventually reference them in other games, and he's had some pretty extensive cameos in GTA 5 and GTA Online.

This appearance in GTA 6 seems a lot less mysterious, given its singular location and how many people have already stumbled on it. But GTA 5's Easter eggs got pretty involved, and I wouldn't be at all surprised if it's just the first step in a wider cryptid mystery. I still need to know if the UFO is going to make a comeback…

#3874. Cartoon-styled "lite-vania" Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh will have you springing yourself, and your summoned pals, from magic jail

Andy Dufresne never thought to use witchcraft, did he

Since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards shows, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.

It looks like this'll be a mix of passively familiar-enhanced punching and more active, mayhaps traditionally Metroid-y power upgrades, Lola's ghastly pals looming over her tiny frame when called upon. It's all presented in a hand-drawn, lightly anime-ish style, complete with a story setup straight out of Saturday morning TV – Lola's only stuck in Skullcatraz because of a summoning-gone-wrong that occurred in pursuit of her school's unlikely Ofsted-compliant 'familiar contest'. I've attended school several times, and will attest that non-sporting contests, which students remain unaware of until seeing a poster for them, do not exist outside of childrens' television*.

This doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

That aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

*Granted, no TV example was ever as egregiously misleading as Jack Black vehicle School of Rock, which convinced me - then a barely-pubescent aspiring bassist - that winning a local Battle of the Bands would pay out thousands in cash, as opposed to the drinks rounds and packs of guitar strings I'd end up competing for a few years later.

#3873. Here's our second wave of PS Plus games for November 2026 - and Sony's scrapping its barely used PC app

Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall!

Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach.

Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November:

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review.

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review.

Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review. It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then.

The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review.

We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review. "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote.

There's plenty to be getting on with, then.

Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

For more information on PlayStation Plus, you can check out our guide to PS Plus and all the available games here.

#3872. Guide: GTA 6: How to Get Ultimate Editon Items & Pre-Order Bonuses

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition features a collection of different items and pre-order bonuses, including vehicles, weapons, and cosmetics. These are unlocked at different points in the story, and some need to be collected from locations around the map. This GTA 6 guide includes step-by-step instructions on how to collect them and when they become available.

On this page: GTA 6: How to Get Ultimate Editon Items & Pre-Order Bonuses

There are 15 extra packs included if you pre-ordered GTA 6's Ultimate Edition. This is where you find them:

You'll find the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak around Jason's House in Key Lento, Mariana County. They're marked on the map, as shown below:

Here's the Dinka Enduro motorcycle underneath Jason's house:

You can also equip a custom Retro livery to Jason's Vapid Ganado by taking it to any Mod Shop, like Coastal Auto Care. Here's what the Retro livery looks like; you'll find it under Pro Builds > Full Kits > Retro Build - Ultimate Edition:

These items are only available in Chapter 1.

An early mission in Chapter 1 will see you go to an Ammu-Nation to purchase a new weapon. Having done so, the Duval Signature ES9 Variant will unlock in the nearby Weapon Locker.

Here's where the mission will take you on the map, with the Duval Signature ES9 Variant for Jason first found there:

The Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is located on Coral Ave, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. Here's how it looks from the outside:

You can set a waypoint under the tabs Style > Tattoos:

Many of the items here are Ultimate Edition exclusive, and marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:

The Goodtime Gear items can be purchased beginning Chapter 1 at The Wonder Whale shop on Sunbelt Hwy, Key Lento, Mariana County. This is how it looks from the outside:

Here's the location on your map. You can also set a marker to the exact store by selecting the Style > Souvenir & Swimwear tabs, as below:

You'll find the Goodtime Gear items inside the shop, on mannequins just left of the entrance:

The Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab, as shown:

You can find One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop just off SR-27 in North Leonard County starting from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:

And here's a map view to help direct you to the right spot:

You can set a waypoint using the menu tabs Vehicles > Mod Shops:

Drive in to the mod shop to find exclusive paint jobs and body work, many of which are exclusive to the Ultimate Edition:

You'll need to have visited South Vice-Dale County before the PTT Youngin$ Illegal Goods robberies unlock starting from Chapter 1. Once you have, you'll find two robberies in and around SW 13th St and El Joven Blvd in Southside.

You can set a waypoint directly to them from the Robberies > Illegal Operations tab in your map:

Take out the gang members inside and loot all the jewelry and drugs before the police arrive:

Then make a quick getaway in your vehicle:

Remember to stow the stolen goods and take them to a nearby fence for cash:

The Rideout Custom Mod Shop is located in Crosstown, Vice City, Vice-Dale County. Here's what it looks like outside:

Note that it's marked with an Ultimated Edition symbol. It can be found under the Vehicles > Mod Shops tab of the map menu:

Take your car here to customise it with all kinds of specialty rims and interiors. Items exclusive to the Rideout Custom Mod Shop will be marked:

You can visit Sara's Unisex Salon from Chapter 1, but Signature styles will not unlock until Chapter 2. Here's what the shop looks like:

And here's its location on your map, which can be found under the Style > Hair & Beauty tab. It's located on Cicada Ave, Hamlet, South Vice-Dale County, Vice-Dale County:

Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:

Stock 305 can be access on NE 15th St, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:

You can find it with the map tabs by selecting Style > Casual & Street:

Inside you'll find Ultimate Edition exclusive clothes for both Jason and Lucia:

You'll get a notification as you progress through Chapter 2 that your '67 Dominator Buggy is available to collect from your Paradise garage, which looks like this:

The Paradise garage is in Watson Bay, Mariana County. Here's its location on your map just in case you get lost:

Get inside the '67 Dominator Buggy to register it. Any current cars you're using will be sent back to one of your other garages automatically:

You'll also unlock some liveries for the '67 Dominator Buggy you can access by taking it to any Pay 'n' Spray.

Shortly after collecting your '67 Vapid Dominator from the Paradise garage, you'll receive a text message on your phone from Wyman telling you about a classic car you can recover and tune up. The message looks like this:

This triggers a new chain of quests under the Exploration tab of your map. To unlock the cars you need to find multiple scraps and WAiNK them so Wyman can collect the parts and restore them.

Go to any Ammunation store around Leonidas and select Manage Weapons at the Weapon Locker, like below:

From Chapter 2 onwards, you'll find the Hawk & Little Morgan in the Revolvers section of both Jason and Lucia's Weapon Locker:

Your Vintage Vice City Pack pre-order bonus will become available shortly after you arrive in Vice City. A marker will appear on your map telling you to visit the familiar Ocean View Hotel in Vice Beach, telling you to pick up your '55 Vapid Stanier, which can be located like below:

The car is unlocked, and once you get inside you'll automatically receive the Shore Court garage as well as new clothes in your wardrobe. A prompt will inform you of this:

You'll also find new hairstyles and more in the Special tab at salons as well as various gun liveries at Ammunation, marked with the Vintage Vice City Pack label:

You can collect your Shitzu Squalo beginning Chapter 4, docked near to Atlantic Ave, Washington Beach, Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County. Here's where you'll find it:

Here's a map view. It's just east of the Y Hotel:

You will find it on the Personal section of your map tabs, but only when you're in a nearby area:

Once you've made progress in Chapter 4, items from the Vice City Style items will be automatically added to your Wardrobe and the Special tab of of most hair salons and tattoo parlours, as below:

You'll get a notification about the '95 Grotti Cheetah upon completing Honest Abe in Chapter 5. Follow the waypoint to Pegassi Residences and go through the main front door, as shown:

Go inside the main entrance and use the lift opposite the entrance:

Your '95 Grotti Cheetah will be parked up and waiting for you to get inside:

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition costs $99.99/£89.99/€99.99. The Standard Edition costs $79.99/£69.99/€79.99.

Yes, I personally think GTA 6's Ultimate Edition is worth it, but it really depends how excited you are for the game and whether you want to get the most out of it.

All of the additional Mod Shops and Stores exclusive to the Ultimate Edition, along with their unique inventory, means you're really adding a lot of cosmetic and personalisation options to the title with the Ultimate Edition.

If you're not the type of player that plans to dress up Jason and Lucia and fiddle with their vehicles, then you may not find value in this.

But it's worth adding that the Classic Car Collection, which adds collectibles quests involving Wyman, are also exclusive to the Ultimate Edition.

You can still enjoy GTA 6 to its fullest without paying for the Ultimate Edition, but you'll get much more out of the game if you do.

Yes, the Ultimate Edition Upgrade can be purchased from the PS Store at any time for $20.00/£20.00/€20.00 and will automatically add all of the extra content to your game once installed.

You'll need to buy the Ultimate Edition Upgrade if you purchase a physical edition of GTA 6, as this content isn't included with the retail release.

If you've followed this guide carefully, then you should now have collected all of your Ultimate Edition items and pre-order bonuses in GTA 6. Congratulations for getting them all!

Remember, you can refer to our GTA 6 guide for a lot more info on the game, including collectibles, walkthroughs, and much more.

GTA 6 is extremely long as games go. It's more comparable to Red Dead Redemption 2's wild west saga than it is to GTA 5, with multiple chapters, missions, and locations you'll move between as you follow Jason and Lucia's story.

As you'll see with the Vintage Vice City Pack and Ultimate Edition bonuses, quite a lot can change between each game's chapter, as you slowly explore the map. So, here's each chapter and mission in GTA 6's main story, plus a little reference summary for each, though some are excluded for spoiler reasons:

Brian, Jason, and Cal track down a broker.

Mattia, Jason, and Lucia have a night out.

Jason, Brian, and Lorrie meet the Kingfishers.

Jason, Lucia, and Dre'Quan see a concert.

Raul invites Jason and Lucia to his base.

Jason and Lucia help with a weapons shipment.

Jason and Lucia run security for a celeb.

Jason, Lucia, and Dre'Quan do a photoshoot.

Lucia helps Cisco confront a porn director.

Jason does some airport baggage handling.

Jason and Dre'Quan steal blackmail material.

#3870. Conan: The Black Pyramid shoves the titular barbarian into a very Hades-inspired action roguelite with the addition of a few other familiar heroes

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

Conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past."

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

#3869. PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away

After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff.

According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.

"Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities".

Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue.

Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely. Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December.

The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026, following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond.

Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles, Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release.

Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May, but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

GTA 6 led the nominations at The Game Awards - but should it even have been eligible in the first place? Rockstar's latest seems a likely candidate to dominate the entire awards season, but opinions on its validity for The Game Awards 2026 seem to vary significantly, so we want to know what you think of this year's frontrunner.

The short version: the nominees for The Game Awards 2026 were announced yesterday, November 17 - two full days before GTA 6 would actually be available for the vast majority of players. Yet despite not having been publicly released, Rockstar's was the most-nominated game of the show, picking up a total of eight nods, with the option for the public to cast their votes on a game that hadn't even been reviewed yet. The response was...confused, to say the least.

Those defending the nominations have a few points in their favor. Possibly the most obvious is the fact that by the time The Game Awards roll around next month, GTA 6 will have spent a few weeks in players' hands. Arguably even more compelling is that The Game Awards are primarily a jury-selected affair, meaning a panel of experts from around the industry - many of whom will have had early access for their GTA 6 review - will have been partly responsible for picking the nominees. Given the glowing reviews that the game's received today, it's safe to say those people think GTA 6 is in GOTY territory.

But on the other hand, public voting does account for some of The Game Awards' selection process. Most people throwing out a vote for GTA 6 in the hours after the nominations were announced would have been doing so before review scores were even unveiled, let alone before getting their own hands on the game. Many others are unlikely to experience the game in full by the time of the awards - unless you're mainlining it over the next couple of weeks, you probably won't have rolled credits without some serious dedication.

Those are the facts of the matter, but what do you think? GTA 6 is pretty much guaranteed to be a mainstay of the awards circuit for the next 12 months, but this is a slightly wonky foot to start that journey off on. You can cast your own vote in the poll at the top of this article, or let us know exactly what your take is in the comments section below.

#3866. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days.

Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds.

It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6, eh?

This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity?

If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

Is the outlaw couple hot together? Or are they running on empty?

In GTA 6 you've got a partner in crime, and it's quite a bit different than it was when you were pulling heists with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in the last game. Jason and Lucia aren't just criminal associates, they're a couple, and their romantic relationship is a big part of the story.

Jason and Lucia can grow closer or more distant, depending on your actions, behavior, and choices. That goes for everything from story missions to random criminal acts to everyday interactions and activities. Here's how Jason and Lucia's romance works in GTA 6.

There are four levels to Jason and Lucia's relationship that can change depending on how you play and the choices you make, one being the lowest and four being the highest. Here are the levels:

When you begin playing as a couple in Chapter 1, your relationship is already a strong one, though it'll still take a while to get it up to 4/4, if that's your goal. Certain actions, activities, and choices will raise your relationship score, and you'll know you've done it when you hear a chime and see a +♥️ appear on the right side of your screen.

Here are just a few actions that will add a ♥️ to your score, and there are plenty more:

*Note: You can't initiate sex whenever you want, but there are multiple times in GTA 6 when a sex scene is available to you, signified by double hearts over your home icon on the map or with certain limited-time onscreen prompts.

What leads to a sex scene? In my playthrough, twice these scenes happened while I was showering as one of the characters and the other asked if they could join me (and you can decide to let them or not). Another was after I reached a major milestone by contributing money to our savings account (hey, financial security is a major turn-on in real life, too!) and there was also a sex scene after a sizable heist. All of these happened while I was at a 4/4 "Hot Together" relationship status.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

You can also lose hearts from your relationship. This didn't happen often in my playthrough, but here's the ones I experienced:

According to Rockstar, if you want a strong relationship in GTA 6, you have to play both sides of that relationship. That means not just playing as Jason and doing nice things for Lucia, but also playing as Lucia and treating Jason well.

For my playthrough, where I reached the end of the game with a 4/4 "Hot Together" status, my stats show that I played nearly the exact same amount of time as Jason as I did Lucia.

Don't worry, this couple isn't joined at the hip. Both Lucia and Jason have missions, storylines, and activities they can (and are sometimes required to) complete alone. You can play plenty of GTA 6 as just a single character running around without the other, just remember to occasionally spend some time with your partner, respond to their texts, and switch to the other character from time to time.

But trust me, you'll want to spend lots of time together. Their relationship is fun to take part in, from both sides. Plus, doing crimes as a couple really pays off. It's helpful to have an extra set of hands to point guns at people, do crowd control during robberies, shoot out a cop's tires while driving, and carry off more loot than you could handle if you were rolling solo.

I'll be honest: I don't know how the game is different if you have a 4/4 relationship or a 1/4 relationship, because I've only played through the story once at this point, and I kept my relationship as strong as possible for nearly the entire game. We'll know more about the effects of a weak relationship as other players experiment with their relationship status, and we'll update this guide with what we find out.

#3863. Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest

Monster Hunter Wilds's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought.

On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

The beta app is the same one those who played the original Wilds beta had in their library. Though the app was removed following the beta's conclusion, because the two share the same ID, the beta should be visible in users' list of played games under the new name. This could mean players won't need to sign up for the supposed Ascendance beta, seemingly only needing to download the new client.

Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

#3862. Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's important because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history."

Perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

We're stuck with 30fps for the time being

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has released to universal acclaim, but as Rockstar fans and developers alike celebrate a monumental release, others begrudge the fact that the game is capped at 30fps instead of the current industry standard of 60fps. If there's any game that gets a pass for 30fps, it's the literal biggest, most technically demanding game ever made, but even so, many are still hoping for an eventual performance mode targeting 60fps. Sadly, according to Rockstar itself, that's impossible even on PS5 Pro due to hardware limitations.

In a statement to Kotaku, Rockstar's technology production director, Marc Chambers, shuts down the idea of GTA 6 running at 60fps any time soon, even on PS5 Pro.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination," says Chambers. "On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR).

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates."

If you're among the many GTA diehards disappointed by 30fps, you can at least take some solace in a technical analysis from Digital Foundry that says GTA 6 is actually "the smoothest GTA game in history" and that every previous GTA was a lot choppier. The analysts found, unsurprisingly, that PS5 Pro is the best way to play it, but even base PS5s and Xbox Series X only dipped occasionally and the dips they suffered were "very minor." Xbox Series S, on the other hand, is another story.

#3859. Cover your robot body in magical fungus aplenty and galavant across a mystical, Soulslike world in MycoRelic, now out in 1.0

Robot, robot, robot, robot, mushroom! Mushroom!

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

#3858. World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunters have found the MMO's first hidden treasure

World of Warcraft secret hunters are a noble breed, known for scouring the MMO for years for hidden trinkets and treasures. With World of Warcraft: Forever's launch, they've uncovered a quest chain for an especially fancy sword.

Over the past week, members of the WoW Secret Hunters Discord found a quest chain that takes place entirely on the Zephras Isle, meaning you'll need to have access to the Skyborne elves to grab this sword. Navigating the island, you'll need to first pick up an ancient heirloom ring from the starting zone. Simple enough!

Then, you'll need to head to Duskwood to gather the Night Watchman's Torch, a handy light source primarily used to light up areas across the darkened woods near Stormwind. It turns out this torch has uses far beyond this one zone however, as taking it back to the Ruins of Ban'aethal on the Zephras Isle will reward you with a secret quest and the Ancient Hilt.

With the hilt and ring, you then must track down an Ancient Blade from one of several spawn locations on the Zephras Isle. Once you finally track it down, that's the end of part one of this quest chain. You get the sword: Eluvi'ana, which on its own isn't particularly strong, but is speculated to be upgraded later down the line.

You then need to get a corrupted water globe from either Darkshore or the Blackfathom Deeps dungeon depending on your faction, do a fetch quest for a hidden spirit in Ashenvale, then take your hoard of special quest items to a NPC in the new Shen'Dralar zone.

He won't give you the finished sword. Instead he sends you to gather more items from higher-level zones. You'll need to raid a secluded vault in Feralas that you can only see with the Ancient Hilt, dive underwater in Azshara, and kill Highborne Shades in Winterspring. Once you've done all that, you can then cleanse the orb up in Hyjal, speak to the fella back in Shen'Dralar, then shimmy over to the end game Dire Maul dungeon to speak to Prince Tortheldrin about *another* sword.

This is how far the World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunter community has gotten to. It's believed that grinding up the Shen'dralar reputation to Honoured is required for the next step, as Prince Tortheldrin pretty much says as much in his dialogue. So the hunt is still on!

These sorts of secrets make up an important part of any good MMO: the solving of mysteries in these vast digital open worlds. In retail WoW, I have fond memories of the Waist of Time quest chain, which was an arduous and comical grind for a fancy belt during the Battle for Azeroth expansion. This secret sword quest chain may very well evolve into something as legendary as that, at least I hope so!

If you're not already playing it, World of Warcraft: Forever is plenty of fun. A record-breaking number of players are making the journey through Azeroth right now, diving into quests and dungeons new and old.

The Fool update has been a huge boost for Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I didn't need anybody to tell me that "Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed" – of course I know him, he's me – but new data from market analysis head Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics certainly puts the depth of the community's devotion into perspective.

In a report, Elliott estimates that developer Mega Crit has sold 7.9 million copies of Slay the Spire 2 through Steam, where it's still in early access. Owner estimations on SteamDB support this figure, ranging from 6.8 million to 7.8 million. But that's not the impressive number. We already knew that Slay the Spire 2 is a massive success and handily the biggest game of its kind.

Here's a truly enviable figure: "The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9M folks have played for over 100 hours," Elliott finds. "That means 24% of the 7.8M player base have put over 100 hours in. About 100K folks have bought Slay the Spire 2 on Steam but haven’t booted up yet, hence the difference between copies and players."

Look under some rocks around Steam stats, PlayStation trophies, or Xbox achievements and you may be horrified to learn that a lot of people don't finish or play very much of the games they buy. A game's average completion time is reliably an entire zip code away from its median playtime. So it's in stats like this that we truly see how Slay the Spire 2 is not only popular, but sticky. Behold, the quantified power of one more run.

"Slay the Spire II has never had fewer than 2.5M active players in a month since launching back in March, and this month is already up on October, thanks to a chunky update that adds a new character," Elliott notes. Additionally, "about 65K absolute nutters (nearly 1% of the player base) have played Slay the Spire II for over 500 hours (!!!)." That is, indeed, an alarmingly large population of absolute nutters. Most games would kill for 1%.

Don't tell my stack of unplayed games, but I'm approaching 300 hours of sequel spire slaying myself, now focusing on Ascension 10 with the new Fool character and having a blast. The update which added The Fool, as well as two entire game modes because Mega Crit is down worse than the Terraria dev team, has evidently seen Slay the Spire 2 jump from around 500,000 daily players back up to a whopping 1.1 million. (Note the key difference between daily active players, or unique players seen in a day, and concurrent players, or players online right now.)

"This is Slay the Spire 2’s highest daily player count in about six months, bringing back 14% of its entire 7.8M-strong player base," Elliott says. "For an opt-in beta branch of an early-access game, that’s some devotion."

That's the kicker, isn't it? This is still a deeply unfinished game which is currently limited to one platform. A 1.0, multiplatform release of Slay the Spire 2 will threaten global productivity in a way not seen since, well, the GTA 6 launch, or before that, Balatro.

#3855. Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at

Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

#3854. As of this week, PlayStation 5 has surpassed 100 million consoles sold

PlayStation 5 has officially surpassed 100m consoles sold, Sony's updated sales data revealed. The milestone was reached on 10th November, almost exactly six years on from the console's launch.

The figure represents 'sell-in' units, meaning those shipped to retailers, as opposed to 'sell-through' which tracks consoles actually sold to consumers. In other words, the number of PS5s in people's homes is smaller than that 100m.

Nevertheless, this is an impressive achievement, and gets the PS5 ever closer to the PS4's 117m, which it achieved by June 2022. It also means the PS5 has almost matched the original PlayStation in units sold (102.4m). As impressive as the numbers are, historical data shows that PS5 sales have been in decline.

Sony hasn't shied away from discussing that fact in its earnings reports. 2.6m PS5 consoles were sold during the most recent quarter (Q2 of FY2026), well below the 4m sold over the same period the year prior. In fact, Q2 of FY2026 is the lowest second quarter on record in terms of units sold since the PS5's launch.

However, it's also worth noting that, small though it may be, the second quarter's result is higher than the first quarter's 1.6m, the second-lowest of any single quarter since the PS5's launch, beaten only by Q4 of FY2025's 1.5m.

If numbers don't recover in the third and fourth quarters, this may be the PS5's lowest year ever in terms of units sold. Although the second quarter's sales boost can be attributed to the high anticipation of Grand Theft Auto 6, the overall downturn is largely due to the console's higher price; Sony raised the PS5 and PS5 Pro's prices on several occasions since 2020. The company's bottom line, however, hasn't been affected much, as its plan to generate more revenue from its already-engaged audience continues to work.

What is a criminal profile, and how does it affect you in GTA 6?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6's criminal profiles (plural, because Jason and Lucia each have their own criminal profile) tracks how you treat other people in the world, reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. How violent you are, how lethal you are in your encounters, and how you treat people and animals in the world will all affect your rating.

There are five levels for Jason and Lucia's criminal profile, represented by "face with horns" emoji-style icons that are shown on your screen:

Your criminal profile is almost entirely dependent on how often you kill people. Try to incapacitate enemies, or wound them instead of killing them, and don't kill too many police or civilians, and you'll wind up with a Professional or Hardened profile. If you're violent for no reason, kill a lot of cops and civilians, and kill pets or defenseless animals, you'll gain a Violent, Psycho, or Irredeemable profile.

Here are the behaviors that will grant you each of the criminal profiles, and the bonuses that come with them:

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (bullet-time)

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (same as Professional)

Bonus: Headshots will increase your focus meter

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Bonus: Headhosts will increase your focus meter, but you will be unable to surrender to cops

If you're a Psycho for too long, you'll gain the Irredeemable profile. While you can move up and down between the other four profiles during the game, once you have an Irredeemable criminal profile, it's permanent.

According to Rockstar, "being irredeemable will have a lasting impact on Jason and Lucia," though we don't yet know what that means. We'll update this guide when we find out.

For my playthrough of the main story, I typically kept both Jason and Lucia in the Professional range, which is the profile I finished the main story with, though I did occasionally drop both of them down to Hardened.

I did this by (mostly) trying to be non-lethal in my encounters, using focus to aim for my enemies' knees and elbows during shootouts. I still killed a whole mess of people in my playthrough.

Here are my endgame stats that achieved me a Professional criminal profile:

*A note on that animal total: I did a little bit of hunting, and I once ran over a cat (by accident!). But most of those animal kills, I suspect, are birds, which have some of the worst AI I've ever seen in a game. They do not get out of the way of cars, trucks, boats, planes, helicopters, ATVs, scooters, and even bicycles. You are going to run over a lot of birds. Sorry.
